title.narrative: Legal Pathways for State and Corporate Accountability across Latin America

description.narrative:
Primary target group: government representatives, diplomats, and legislators engaged in the UN Binding Treaty negotiations and in the development of national laws on business, human rights, and environmental protection in Latin America.
Secondary target group: civil society organizations, human rights and environmental defenders, national human rights institutions, and affected communities advocating for stronger corporate accountability and the protection of people and nature.

The overall objective is to strengthen political commitment to a robust and effective UN Binding Treaty on Business and Human Rights, while advancing complementary national legal frameworks across Latin America that safeguard human rights and protect the environment.
The project aims to increase engagement by Latin American States in the treaty negotiations, foster regional coordination, and build broader governmental support for a binding international instrument that prevents state and corporate abuses, guarantees access to justice, and ensures effective remedies for affected communities. At the national level, the initiative will promote advocacy and policy dialogue to advance binding legislation aligned with international standards, reinforcing accountability and the protection of people, communities, and nature.
